judgements.reason: Photograph viewed 2026-11-24: looking up the smooth mottled trunk of a London plane into its summer crown, a line of trees along a mown field, the stepped base of a flagpole at the left, school buildings behind, daylight, colour. Re-judged the same morning: an earlier run held it not_special, reading the site as a school field. The GPS fix stands in Stewart Reid Memorial Park, Ngahinapouri: land given in 1946 in memory of pilot officer Stewart Reid and planted with 34 memorial trees, one per local man who served in WWII (NZHistory). The flagpole on its stepped base in the photo is the park's. A mature plane in a war-memorial park is somewhat special. Live as ngahinapouri/ngh_001 under the closed list (Hidde, 2026-11-17); the story does not claim it is one of the 34.

known as “Mahakali Vad” or “Mini Kabirvad”-is believed to be around 400 to 700 years old and ranks among Gujarat's largest banyan trees.
Spreading across roughly half an acre with a dense network of aerial roots and trunks, it houses a shrine to Goddess Mahakali beneath its canopy and has been developed as a religious and nature tourism destination in the region.

judgements.tree: The Great Lawn Plane of Parc Montsouris
judgements.reader_note:
This tree has a beautiful heart-shaped crown. 

It stands in the central field. Given its circumference, it seems likely that it has been there since the park opened. If so, it has witnessed the parties in the early 1900s thrown by the artist, who received the key to the park from the park ranger, so he could have fun there with his friends. 

« Le Jardin », poem by Jacques Prévert, in Paroles :
Des milliers et des milliers d'années
Ne sauraient suffire
Pour dire la petite seconde d'éternité
Où
